name: Lender tranche inspections
one_liner: Remote, AI-verified construction progress checks that let housing lenders release tranches faster and cheaper.
why: It has the clearest payer: lenders already spend money on every stage inspection, the job recurs on every under-construction loan, and ULI gives a standard rail to plug into. Unlike contractor tools, it sells to a few dozen institutions rather than thousands of small firms.

why_not_others.name: POD-to-payment autopilot (freight trucking)
why_not_others.reason: A close second with strong pain, but thousands of small buyers and the risk that shippers still demand paper originals. Worth a parallel 2-week interview sprint.

why_not_others.name: RFQ-to-quote copilot (MSME manufacturing)
why_not_others.reason: Real demand, but each shop's cost model needs calibration, which slows the first 10 customers.

riskiest_assumption: Lenders will accept geotagged photo evidence plus AI checks in place of (or before) a physical visit by an empanelled engineer.

test.method: Interview technical or credit heads at 8 housing finance companies, then run 20 inspections in parallel with their physical visits.
test.success_signal: 3 lenders agree to a paid pilot; AI verdict matches the engineer's in 90% of cases

why_industry: Construction scored highest in the industry scan: money is visibly stuck behind paperwork and inspections, compliance recurs every quarter, and few AI products serve it. Within it, lenders are the easiest buyers: a few dozen institutions with budgets, not thousands of small contractors.
